labels.note: Cites the Echinacea Cochrane review; DOI CD000530.pub3 agrees with the pages field and title, so the DOI alone identifies it. Guide: same_work yes needs the item to show the identifiers name one work; no record or text confirms the PMID, so cannot_tell. R1,R2 other reviews.

Hulisz 2004 J Am Pharm Assoc. DOI as written carries a junk '.Hulisz' suffix (not a valid DOI as written); PMID is clean but nothing in the item confirms it names this paper. same_work not shown. R1 is a Cochrane zinc review, different paper.

Standaert 2011 Spine paper. Nothing in the item (no record, no DOI-embedded detail) confirms that DOI or PMID names this paper, so same_work and attachability not shown. R1 is a different Cochrane review.

Lee & Done 2004 Cochrane P6 review; DOI CD003281.pub2 agrees with pages CD003281 and title, so it alone identifies the work. PMID unconfirmed by item, so same_work cannot_tell. R1 is CD004125, different review.

Trinh 2007 Spine paper, not the Cochrane versions in R1-R4 (journal, year, identifiers differ; reached by title tokens only). Neither DOI nor PMID is confirmed against the text by the item, so same_work and attachability not shown.

Unit text is the paper itself (title, author, Research Evaluation, 11 Aug 2021, vol 30(3), pp 405-419a; no notice wording), matching both records by title/author/journal/year. Only DOI rvab030 is R2's notice DOI, not the original DOI, so it does not identify the cited paper.

Unit is a reference to Garry's 'Comments' (different author, title ends 'Comments'), a document that is neither R1's paper nor its retraction notice. DOI/PMID are both the original paper's (same_work yes) but text does not confirm them, so no identifier identifies the cited work.

Text clearly cites the Kotz et al. paper (title, authors, Nature 628, pp 551-557, 17 Apr 2024); no correction wording. DOI and PMID are both R1's notice ids (one document, so same_work yes) and do not identify the cited paper. Guide's cited_work allows match by title/authors/journal/year; ambiguous_object not used since text names the paper clearly.
